title: Halcyon Telecom pilot outreach journal
content:
Purpose
- Keep a running personal journal for Halcyon Telecom account outreach and pilot planning. This is rough; use to iterate emails, objection responses, and pilot KPIs.

Quick account snapshot
- Company: Halcyon Telecom (regional carrier, mid-size, heavy B2B focus)
- HQ: Denver, CO
- Estimated engineering org: ~120 engs; cloud-first but some on-prem for legacy BSS
- Priority: customer support automation, reducing MTTR for network incidents, embedding LLM into partner portal for config guidance

Key personas and leads (notes from LinkedIn / calls)
- Leah Moreno — Head of AI/ML (decision influencer). Prior at Netwave, cares about model explainability and safety.
- Connor Briggs — Director, Platform Engineering (technical buyer). Manages infra decisions, cost/RPO-sensitive.
- Sabrina Lee — Head of Partnerships (buying champion for reseller integrations). Motivated by faster partner onboarding.
- Marcus Yoon — Security Architect (will drive compliance ask). SSO, KMS, audit trails are gating items.

Observed constraints / red flags
- Preference for vendor solutions that can run inside customer VPC (data residency).
- Long procurement cycles for anything that touches customer data; asks for SOC2 + monthly security reviews.
- Concern about latency for interactive troubleshooting flows used by support agents.
- Existing tooling: Zendesk + internal knowledge base; some homegrown orchestration for configs.

Elevator pitch (1 sentence)
- Redwood gives Halcyon predictable, production-grade LLM inference that you can run inside your VPC or reserved capacity, so partner-facing tutorials and support triage are faster and cheaper without exposing PII.

Top objections and short scripts
- "We can't send customer data to third parties."
  Response: "Totally understood. We can run Redwood Private inside your VPC or on-prem package; keys stay in your KMS and audit logs are customer-side. Many carriers we've worked with do this during pilot. I'll share a checklist for the technical review."

- "How do we control costs with LLMs?"
  Response: "Redwood Optimize recommends batching/caching and model quantization settings per workload. For the pilot we can target a configuration that meets your latency SLO while keeping per-token costs under an agreed threshold; we'll run a small load test to validate."

- "We're concerned about model hallucinations in config guidance."
  Response: "We include structured tool-calling patterns and deterministic reranking for factual answers. Also propose a supervised rollout: human-in-the-loop initially and narrow prompt templates tied to your KB. We can create regression tests against representative prompts."

Sample outbound sequence (multi-touch, tailored)
1) Cold email (short)
Subject: Halcyon x Redwood — pilot to cut partner onboarding time
Hi Leah — noticed Halcyon's partner portal rollout. We help carriers embed production LLMs with on-prem/VPC options to cut partner onboarding and support MTTR. Would you be open to a 20-minute call to explore a small pilot?
2) Follow-up (3 days)
Subject: Quick idea to cut partner onboarding by X weeks
Hi Leah — adding a quick example: a 6-week pilot we ran for a regional carrier reduced time-to-first-integration by ~40% using an LLM-powered integration assistant. happy to share the pilot plan.
3) Objection handling/Proof email (7 days)
Subject: Security + SLA plan for pilots
Hi Leah — attaching an outline: VPC deployment, KMS integration, SOC-like checklist + sample trace for audit. If MCC/Platform want a technical RFC, Connor and I can run a short workshop next week.

Call script (first discovery call, 20 mins)
- 0-3m: quick intros (name, role), confirm agenda
- 3-8m: problem framing (ask Sabrina about partner onboarding pain, ask Connor about latency/cost targets)
- 8-12m: show 2 concisely phrased use cases: 1) partner onboarding assistant (config templates, validation), 2) support triage (KB -> suggested fixes)
- 12-16m: security & deployment options (VPC, dedicated, private); surface Marcus's anticipated asks
- 16-20m: propose next step: scoping workshop + pilot success metrics

Pilot proposal (6-week, low-friction)
- Weeks 0-1: kickoff & security questionnaire; grant temporary access or define VPC path; identify 1 pilot integration flow + sample prompt set.
- Weeks 2-3: minimal integration (server-side API integration to staging partner portal); baseline metrics collected.
- Weeks 4-5: tuning (batching, caching, quantization), human-in-loop checks, run 2 stress scenarios.
- Week 6: deliverables: metrics report, small runbook for production rollout, decision review.

Success metrics (suggested)
- Functional: partner onboarding time reduced by >=30% for pilot workflows.
- SLOs: 95th percentile response latency <150ms for single-turn retrieval+generate in staging; tail detection for longer sessions.
- Cost: average per-inference cost < $0.0015 (negotiable) or keep within agreed budget.
- Quality: accuracy on structured config extraction > 92% (eval set of 200 prompts).

Integration checklist (technical)
- Decide deployment mode: Hosted w/ VPC peering vs Redwood Private in Halcyon account vs Dedicated reserved pool.
- Auth: SSO + API tokens; KMS integration details (must support AWS KMS and HSM in future).
- Logging: what logs stay customer-side; define retention and redaction needs.
- Traceability: mapping request IDs to internal incident IDs for auditing.
- Network: egress rules, ports, and proxy requirements.
- Data: sample payload types, PII handling, and KB sync cadence.

Potential pilot risks and mitigations
- Risk: procurement stalls on legal/security review. Mitigation: pre-send SOC2 summary + security checklist; offer staging-only data path.
- Risk: latency in production > target. Mitigation: propose dedicated pool + kernel tuning; fall back to lightweight reranking model for tail.
- Risk: integration burden for partner portal. Mitigation: build a small adapter + example middleware; Redwood dev time offered for first integration sprint.

Open questions to chase before workshop
- Leah: confirm top 2 partner workflows to prioritize and expected reduction targets.
- Connor: will infra allow a short-lived VPC peering or prefer private deployment?
- Marcus: sample security questionnaire items (need example for KMS/HSM, logging retention).
- Sabrina: pilot success decision owner and timeline for procurement.

Next tactical steps (my personal TODO)
- [ ] Draft short technical RFC for Connor (use repo linked above) — due 2025-02-03
- [ ] Pull SOC2 summary + security checklist from Confluence and attach to follow-up email — due 2025-01-22
- [ ] Warm intro request to Sabrina via mutual contact (Jonah to check) — due 2025-01-20
- [ ] Prepare short demo script and canned prompts (half-day build) — due 2025-02-07
- [ ] Schedule discovery workshop with Leah/Connor/Marcus (aim for week of 2025-02-10)

Notes to self (voice memo style)
- Be explicit about deployment options early — this reduces procurement pushback.
- Quantify cost per inference in the email only if you can commit to the number for pilot.
- Offer a fixed-scope deliverable at pilot end: runbook + decision memo.

Slack snippets to paste in channel when needed
- "Heads up: planning Halcyon Telecom pilot. Need SOC2 summary + KMS checklist triage. @security can you pull the short doc?"
- "Partner champion: Sabrina Lee. Can someone intro? Jonah said he has a contact. Thanks!"

Archive of prior outreach attempts (keeps brief)
- 2025-01-19: cold email sent to Leah (no reply)
- 2025-01-22: follow-up email + security note sent to Leah + Connor
- 2025-01-24: Jonah left voicemail for Sabrina; left brief message referencing demo

End journal entry
- Will iterate the outbound sequence after workshop prep. Keep this file as my single source of truth for Halcyon messaging and pilot metrics.
